name: Alt-right
summary: A loose, largely online white-nationalist and identitarian movement that emerged around 2008-2016, holding that white (European) identity is under attack from multiculturalism, egalitarianism and liberal elites. It favours racial separation or an ethnostate, sharply restricted immigration, nationalism and anti-globalism, and it rejects Enlightenment equality and the conservative establishment. Economics is a minor concern, with protectionist leanings.
scope: The mainstream white-nationalist 'Alternative Right' of 2010-2017 associated with Richard Spencer, Greg Johnson and Jared Taylor, with the Daily Stormer as its harder edge. It excludes the 'alt-lite' civic-nationalist wing and the paleoconservatism it grew from. Because the movement had no program, answers on economics and social issues are mostly low-confidence inferences.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The movement rejects Enlightenment universal rights and equality, so it would not favour entrenched universal guarantees; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of anti-colonial and egalitarian norms, and its defence of European heritage and borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: Spencer-style elitism favours rule by a European elite rather than mass democracy, though the movement has no monarchy program.

minority-veto.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarian democracy and treats minority consent claims as irrelevant; inferred from its anti-Enlightenment stance.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is elitist and authoritarian in outlook but has no doctrine on resistance to rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is hostile to liberal democratic institutions and has no settled view on the monarch versus parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No common line; the movement is a loose online grouping and animal welfare is not a part of its identity.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the typical conservative-adjacent view that animal use is acceptable; no movement doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Spencer-style elitism holds that elites owe duties to their own people; inferred, not a stated line.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is activist and aims at metapolitics and a political order for its people, so withdrawal is contrary to its aims.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement blames mainstream media and culture for shaping opinion to the liberal order; inferred from its attacks on the media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's metapolitical focus on culture as a source of power and its attack on liberal elites.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; the movement holds economics to be secondary and has no common line on world-system theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist and ethnostate stance, which reserves political life for the native people.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable; the movement has no stance on communist party independence.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The movement favours nationalism and protectionist economics; inferred preference for national self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from irredentist strands of European nationalism that the movement draws on; not a stated program.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement holds that white people should lead their own countries and rejects the idea that indigenous status should confer rule over settler descendants.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The movement rejects anti-fascism and treats it as an enemy; inferred from its hostility to the left.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement's attitude to fascism is sympathetic or ambiguous and its adherents are strongly anti-communist, so they would not condemn both as equals.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The movement defends Confederate heritage and the Lost Cause narrative; inferred from the movement's focus on defence of white Southern identity.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The movement defends Confederate and similar monuments as part of European heritage, and attacks their removal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The movement is anti-feminist and treats men's disadvantage as neglected; inferred from its views on gender roles.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anti-feminist views prominent in the movement hold that men are under-served in domestic violence; inferred from its stance on gender.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement rejects universalism and holds that different peoples need their own institutions, which supports the view; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between authoritarian and anti-state strains.

paid-care-work.rationale: The movement favours traditional gender roles and does not support paying domestic labour as a policy.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement traditionalist, family-oriented outlook.

office-by-exam.rationale: Adherents split: elitist rhetoric favours rule by the capable, but the movement has no civil-service program.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the protectionist and nationalist leanings noted for the movement.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the movement rejection of liberal social change and focus on family and fertility.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the movement rejection of egalitarian democracy in favour of elite leadership.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The movement has no common economic line.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from its defence of property and rejection of communal ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: No documented position; the movement is sceptical of liberal democracy but has no budget program.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its ethnonationalism, which makes a single national culture and language the norm.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its ethnonationalist aim of keeping the homeland in the nation hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and treats group disparities as natural rather than discriminatory.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Adherents split: some praise tradition over consumer culture, others the market; no common line.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, non-interventionist stance of Spencer and the movement.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, non-interventionist stance of the movement.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: the movement's anti-elite stance includes hostility to donor-driven politics, but it has no economic programme.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: nationalists in the movement view foreign-funded groups as a threat to national identity.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Spencer and others want white birth rates raised and immigration cut.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the movement's ethnostate aim implies restricting land to the ethnic community.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: no common economic line, but the movement is hostile to welfare statism for non-whites.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Spencer rejects Enlightenment universalism and democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: it prizes order and hierarchy, but disclaims loyalty to the existing regime; adherents lean to reject a duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposed interventionist wars and favoured an America First line.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement is documented as promoting the claim that Jews and other minorities conspire against white identity.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist and pronatalist, it would uphold marriage as an institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: protectionism and nationalist localism fit its anti-globalism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the movement is mostly online and informal, but leaders also built organisations and conferences.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: anti-globalism and nationalism favour national sovereignty over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: the movement defines the nation by race, not religion, and many members are secular or pagan.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its ethnonationalism and anti-globalism, which reject submission to other powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred; the movement is nationalist and offers no common line on regional fiscal questions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and does not discuss common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to egalitarianism and the left, though it also criticises Cold War anti-communism of the conservative establishment.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No common economic line; Spencer backed state health care for white welfare while others favour markets.

religion-illusion.rationale: Views vary; Spencer and Johnson are critical of Christianity but treat religion and heritage as identity markers, not mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Economics is a minor concern with protectionist leanings, and the movement is split between admirers and critics of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and favours traditional gender roles, not economic transformation for equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its advocacy of traditional gender roles and family-based care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred; cultural-purity themes suggest sympathy but there is no documented policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its majoritarian ethnonationalism, which gives minority nations within the state little standing.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, elitist stance and focus on a racial ethnostate rather than common-property communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its aim of ethnic homogeneity and white demographic dominance; there is no specific programme of settling minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of both liberal capitalism and egalitarian leftism in favour of identity-based nationalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement holds that European peoples have an ancestral right to their lands and an ethnostate, as Spencer and Johnson state.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial and minimisation circulate in the movement, and the Daily Stormer is openly denialist, though Spencer has equivocated.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The movement has no single line; the 'alt-lite' accepts gay members while the harder edge opposes it. Not stated in the sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement rejects liberal democracy and egalitarianism, and Spencer attacks the media; suppression of opponents is inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement is mostly secular or pagan-leaning and not interested in enforcing a state religion; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Economic ties to colonies are not an issue the movement addresses; it is anti-globalist and favours its own nation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to Islam and Muslim immigration.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secularism and hostility to Islam.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarian democracy and favours elite rule.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement rejects Enlightenment equality and treats race as the main category.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Spencer and the movement hold traditional gender roles and oppose transgender recognition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not stated; Spencer's views on health care and life are mixed, so adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Spencer and Johnson say left and right are both outdated and put identity first.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of Marxism and focus on race over class.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement holds that Islam and Muslim immigration threaten European identity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement is mostly secular or pagan and does not ground authority in God; Spencer's elite rule is its own basis.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not an issue the movement addresses; adherents split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to feminist-style and corporate-protection measures; not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement leans protectionist and nationalist in economics and rejects laissez-faire, but is not a social-market movement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement is nationalist and militarist-friendly, so abolishing armed forces is rejected; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalist, protectionist leanings.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement is anti-globalist and opposed to foreign entanglements, so staying out of blocs fits; Spencer's Trump-era stance is non-interventionist.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not a defining issue; the movement favours hierarchy and elites but has no stated position on dynastic rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to egalitarian and left-wing economics; the sources do not discuss cooperative banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalist, anti-globalist stance, which opposes outside institutions setting national policy.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement rejects equality but wants an ethnic, not property, qualification; the sources show no common line on property franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of feminism, egalitarianism and environmental left politics, which it treats as part of the liberal elite agenda.

reification.rationale: A Marxist idea; the movement is hostile to Marxism and treats race and identity, not class relations, as the basic social fact.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The movement attacks liberal media bias and elites but is not anti-wealth and holds no common line on press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement favours authority and an ethnostate; it prizes strong rulers but has no stated position on rule by standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement seeks a white ethnostate and restricted citizenship by race, which is its defining aim.

online-participation.rationale: The movement organised largely online but has no stated line on mass online political participation, and many adherents favour elite rule.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the movement's distrust of institutions and mild preference for strong rulers over transparency; the sources do not address it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement is focused on race rather than religion and its adherents vary on religious questions, so the sources do not settle it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement's targets are racial and ethnic, and its figures have criticised some boycotts, but its antisemitic fringe backs them, so adherents are split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the movement's elitist, anti-egalitarian outlook; it is anti-establishment but never proposed lot-selected assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Adherents split between pagan or secular members and Christian traditionalists; the sources do not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's lack of an economic programme; some attack globalist elites while others defend capitalists.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to progressive social causes and its traditionalist, hierarchical outlook.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: the movement is mostly secular or pagan, but its emphasis on traditional European culture makes state-imposed atheism unlikely to be favoured.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its demand for order and a strongly enforced ethnic state; abolition runs against its authoritarian leanings.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of multiculturalism and egalitarianism in favour of racially homogeneous states.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: adherents are split between free-market and welfare-for-whites positions, and the movement has no stated view.

term-limits.rationale: The movement has no stated position on term limits and its adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of egalitarian liberal democracy and preference for elite or authoritarian rule over participatory schemes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; adherents' concerns centre on demographic rather than extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist views on gender roles and hierarchy.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist, patriarchal view of the family.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement wants an ethnostate and sharply restricted immigration, so non-citizen voting is rejected.

rent-control.rationale: Economics is a minor concern for the movement and it has no common line.

abolish-ip.rationale: No common line; economics is a minor concern.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the movement has some interest in discipline and ritual but no programme for this.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear line.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and anti-globalism; Spencer criticised foreign interventions.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The movement rejects 'guilt' narratives about white nations; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The movement is not concerned with the question; economics has no common line.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement rejects Enlightenment egalitarianism and its figures celebrate force; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Identitarians treat European identity as continuous from ancient origins; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and holds biological, hierarchical views of sex and race.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist and anti-egalitarian outlook.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from nationalist and identitarian cult of heroes of the people; not a stated position.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Adherents range from neo-pagans to Christians; no common view.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: it wants a homeland that gathers the people in an ethnostate.

culture-before-state.rationale: Greg Johnson's metapolitical strategy holds that cultural and ideological change must precede political power.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of egalitarianism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its ethnonationalism that economic life should favour the national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its ethnostate aim, which would unite people of one stock in one unit.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no labour programme and economics is a minor concern; adherents are split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Class power is not an alt-right concern, and its egalitarianism-hostile elitism rejects workers' rule; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Economics is a minor concern with protectionist leanings; no common line on public services.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement has no program on legislative design, though it rejects mass democracy; adherents differ.

municipal-property.rationale: Community ownership is not an alt-right theme; inferred from its nationalist and elitist outlook.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Spencer's call for a single ethnostate implies a unified state, not confederations of local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Spencer and the movement favour traditional gender roles and family, which makes a family wage congenial; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between technocratic and traditionalist outlooks.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: No stated position on ageing research; inferred indifferent.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No stated position; the movement is split between wanting free-speech finance tools and favouring state power.

online-anonymity.rationale: The movement grew online and relied on pseudonymous accounts, so it defends anonymity for itself; inferred from its history.

person-over-state.rationale: Johnson and Spencer put the racial collective and ethnostate above the individual and reject Enlightenment equality; inferred from their quoted views.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Spencer is secular-leaning while Johnson and others discuss religion and paganism; adherents split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No stated position; the movement favours an ethnostate but has no settled view on regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: No stated position; economics is a minor concern.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement is hostile to cosmopolitan urban life and its multiculturalism; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Spencer and Johnson explicitly state that whites have distinct racial interests and should organise for them, notably through an ethnostate.

racial-pride.rationale: Spencer's 'Hail our people' speech and the movement's identitarian stance make white pride central.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The alt-right opposed neoconservative interventionism and foreign wars, favouring nationalist restraint.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the alt-right defines peoples by race and ancestry, not language, so a language-based nation across borders is not its test.

communal-electorates.rationale: The alt-right rejects multicultural group politics and wants one ethnically defined polity or ethnostate, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: it speaks of elites and migration undermining the white nation, but not of foreign powers partitioning the country.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the movement is hostile to universities as bastions of egalitarianism and has no tuition programme.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: it is anti-globalist, sceptical of climate policy and opposes new taxes and international regimes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: it speaks of securing a future for white children, but not of environmental stewardship.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses sex differences and traditional roles, but not giving women's values more weight in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: nationalists favour strong national defence, and the movement opposes liberal internationalist arms treaties.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; the movement is anti-establishment but did not address treaty secrecy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: protectionist and anti-globalist leanings imply support for state control of capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants a strong ethnostate but its gun-rights and militia-friendly strands split on disarming private groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and authoritarian, hierarchical outlook; it criticised foreign wars but not by endorsing mutiny.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: economics is a minor concern and it is hostile to egalitarian left institutions, though protectionist strands court workers.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: no shared economic line; welfare for whites is accepted by some, redistribution by the state criticised by others.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: it prefers a strong sovereign state to rules binding it, and has no developed fiscal doctrine.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: it opposes globalism but is hostile to aid and rebalancing in favour of the developing world.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: it attacks the liberal establishment yet wants a strong state of its own, so takes it over rather than abolishing it; adherents split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it wants a unified, homogeneous nation under a single order rather than communities freely trying different systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: no environmental programme; some strands favour romantic conservation, but pricing nature is not a theme.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its core theme is the white nation or people as a community with a shared destiny, as in Spencer's 'Hail our people' rhetoric.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: it opposes liberal egalitarian redistribution and has no program of debt relief.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: it rejects colonial-exploitation framings of this kind as part of the left's grievance politics.

shared-human-nature.rationale: It rejects Enlightenment egalitarianism and universal human equality in favour of innate racial difference.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: it treats mainstream media as a hostile liberal establishment, so state-funded media is not valued.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Spencer and Johnson treat religion as secondary to race and some, like Spencer, reject Christianity as a universal creed; a shared universal truth runs against particularist identity.

farm-price-support.rationale: Economics is a minor concern with protectionist leanings, so farm support is plausible but never stated as a movement position.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nationalist and strength-oriented, the movement would not favour unilateral disarmament; inferred from its nationalism, not stated.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement has no labour programme and Spencer rejects class politics in favour of racial identity; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: A conservative-traditionalist, anti-multicultural stance suggests support for banning a practice associated with immigrant communities; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Spencer favoured traditional gender roles and a patriarchal order, but equal inheritance is not discussed; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Treating European peoples as one nation with one heritage, the movement would see shared tongues as unified; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No stated view; adherents range from anti-regulation to ethnonationalist environmentalists.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, anti-egalitarian outlook that hereditary traditional authority is respected, but chiefs are a non-Western institution it never addresses.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmentalism is not a defining concern; some strands link it to blood-and-soil nationalism while others are indifferent.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Its law-and-order, authoritarian leaning suggests support for fixed sentences; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: With an ethnostate and sharply restricted immigration as its core aim, it would demand assimilation or exclusion; the language requirement itself is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Alt-right writers address labour mostly through nationalism and protectionism; no stated stance on compulsory union membership, so adherents are split; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Movement figures backed Trump's claims about voter fraud and restrictive immigration; inferred from that emphasis.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement defines itself around European and often Christian-heritage identity and rejects pluralism; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The alt-right rejects egalitarian liberal democracy and favours an ethnically defined state, so competitive elections alone do not make a government legitimate to them.

premarital-sex.rationale: Adherents hold traditionalist views on sex roles though attitudes differ across the online movement; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The movement relies on the internet and complains of platform censorship; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economics is a minor concern, with protectionist leanings and no endorsement of libertarian cash-transfer schemes; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anti-feminist and anti-egalitarian themes run through the movement, and some factions call for restricting women's franchise, but this is not a program position; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Adherents hold that feminism and not religion drives women's status; inferred from the movement's anti-feminism.

race-social-construct.rationale: White-nationalist adherents hold that race is a biological reality and the basis of nations, as Spencer and Johnson state.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement's anti-feminism and rejection of egalitarianism make adherents opposed to state gender-equality bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The movement has no property doctrine and economics is a minor concern, so first-claim ownership is not a shared position.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and anti-globalism; the movement rejects authority above the nation and liberal international institutions.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Spencer and Johnson are openly secular or pagan-leaning and hostile to Christianity's egalitarianism, though some adherents are Christian; inferred and split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of egalitarianism and its traditional gender-role views, which Spencer's views support.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from hostility to communism and the leftist elites the movement opposes; no source states a position on planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Spencer is critical of democracy but no source records a call for indirect election, so adherents are not shown to hold a view.

national-church-status.rationale: Adherents are split between Christian traditionalists and pagan or secular members, and the movement has no line on church status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement seeks racial separation or an ethnostate rather than autonomy for minorities inside a shared state; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favours national self-determination of ethnic groups but has no stated position on local plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is concerned with ethnic homelands rather than colonial borders, and adherents are split.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the movement's embrace of strength, tradition and abundance for its people; not an alt-right theme.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred ethnonationalism cuts both ways between protecting homelands and favouring dominant groups.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalist gender roles and rejection of egalitarianism, which favour men-only drafts.

notes: The movement had no formal program and splintered after Charlottesville (2017). Strands differ on Jews, Christianity, and an ethnostate versus a white-majority nation. Only one primary source (speech excerpts) could be opened; most of the primary writings were inaccessible.
